name: Nahshon
title: Leader of the tribe of Judah
summary: Nahshon, son of Amminadab, was the leader of the tribe of Judah during the wilderness journey after leaving Egypt. He is known as a prominent figure in Israel's early history and is an important part of the lineage leading to King David and ultimately Jesus Christ. According to Jewish tradition, he was the first to step into the Red Sea in faith before it parted.

keyEvents.title: Leader of the tribe of Judah at the census
keyEvents.description: Nahshon was appointed as head of the tribe of Judah during the first census in the wilderness, leading a tribe of 74,600 men.

keyEvents.title: Camp arrangement around the tabernacle
keyEvents.description: Nahshon and the tribe of Judah were given the foremost position in the camp arrangement, east of the tabernacle, and were the first tribe to break camp when the Israelites traveled.

keyEvents.title: Dedication Offering for the Altar
keyEvents.description: Nahshon was the first leader to bring his offering at the dedication of the altar in the tabernacle, on the first day.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in Judah's Lineage
keyEvents.description: Nahshon is mentioned as an important part of Judah's lineage, a descendant of Perez and predecessor to Boaz and David.

keyEvents.title: Relative of Aaron
keyEvents.description: Nahshon's sister Elisheba was married to the high priest Aaron, linking the tribe of Judah to the priestly office in the tribe of Levi.

keyEvents.title: In Jesus' Genealogy
keyEvents.description: Nahshon is mentioned in the genealogy of Jesus Christ in both the Gospels of Matthew and Luke, as a key link in the messianic line.
